_all.blocker: Gemini CLI 0.34.0 refuses to start with the owner's stored Google login: IneligibleTierError: "This client is no longer supported for Gemini Code Assist for individuals. To continue using Gemini, please migrate to the Antigravity suite of products" (captured 2026-11-24 on the qualification machine; no request reached Mind Place).
_all.fallback: Antigravity CLI (separate row). Gemini CLI on an eligible (for example Workspace or paid) account is covered by owner card 'any local CLI that failed in the agent run'.
_all.note: Not a Mind Place defect: the vendor client did not start a session.

_all.reason: Claude web and desktop custom connectors need an HTTPS MCP URL reachable by Claude. Release 1 ships no general public gateway (only the OpenAI-only secure tunnel). An agent cannot sign in to the owner's Claude account or publish an endpoint.

Hosted ChatGPT needs the owner's OpenAI tunnel ID and runtime API key and ChatGPT developer mode. Those credentials must not be handled by an agent. An earlier real-ChatGPT run of search, fetch and context_build over the tunnel (MP-7MCP-04 baseline) was on an older build and is not claimed for this SHA.

Hosted Gemini needs the owner's account (Connect to an MCP server or Developer Mode) and an HTTPS endpoint reachable by Gemini. The Gemini app custom-app feature is reported to require an eligible personal account; if the owner's account is not eligible the result is PROVIDER_BLOCKED, to be recorded on the card.

Antigravity CLI 1.5.10 reached the listener and sent initialize, which Mind Place correctly refused with 401: its MCP configuration does not expand environment variables in headers, so the literal placeholder was sent. Delivering the key would require putting it literally on a command line or in its shared user config (~/.gemini/config), which this harness deliberately does not do. Headless runs also stay in request-review permission mode ('--mode auto' is not available for this account), so tool calls would wait for approval. See receipt blocked-antigravity.json.
